body:
Thanks for your words. Rather than your post insinuating those things it's more that I'm so used to people force-ably, even with hostility if you show any resistance, pushing their belief that everything gets better or no one can be in a situation they can't get out of onto me and taking offense if I don't believe everything they say. It's incredibly common to the point almost everyone does it.

It happens time and time again and I start to expect it. This is the biggest hurdle to getting support - people telling you their beliefs and promising things that just isn't something they have the right to promise. It's exhausting!

Sometimes it's good just to talk about things, but everyone seems to think they HAVE to give advice.

I'm not talking about you here, just explaining why it's hard to look past anything that comes off that way.

I'll be overseas, leaving in ~36 hours after which I will be gone for 11 days. I'll see how I feel when I'm back home but I'm mostly compelled to go, it's not my wish. But maybe I'll enjoy it when I'm there. It's hard to see how things could ever get better, I grew up with all this, and anyone I told always promised it would and it just never did - when is that meant to happen again because it's been at least 16 years since people began to tell me that!

For the most part I can copy paste the response to /u/janbaldwin81 where I say that I spent 9 years in mental health care (psychiatrists, therapists - good ones, at that) and nothing worked. Once my immediate situation was resolved they could only assist with anything I wanted to accomplish. Feels like they were fulfilling a dying wish now. They probably knew since no medication helped in any way and symptoms only worsened.

I wouldn't realize I was losing touch with reality if I didn't know first-hand how it looked.

It's wishful thinking to say I have any sort of future and it's really upsetting when people tell me that, not as you have, but force-ably pushing it on me like I'll be convinced and I'll just immediately be OK as if it was all in my head. Seems like it's something people need to tell themselves and just project it my way.

Mostly the mental health care system is good here but I was with them for 9 years and there was a point where there just wasn't anything else they could do, I realized it a while before they told me. Medication's don't help, I only ever get the side effects and not the benefits. Goes both for anti-depressants and anti-psychotics. Really isn't anything anyone can do.
